subject: Renewal pricing proposal: temporary shelf + staged step-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jason Lee <jason.lee@greenline.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 31 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal pricing proposal: temporary shelf + staged step-up

Hi Jason,

Thanks again for taking the time last week. Per our conversation I put together a concise proposal that aims to preserve Greenline's unit economics through the immediate renewal window while giving you a clear, capacity-forward path if usage accelerates. High level: simple temporary shelf, a modest step-up commit, and a limited credit to offset onboarding spike risk.

Proposal (summary)
- Temporary price shelf (months 0-3): hold current list rates so your effective per-token cost does not increase at renewal.
- Staged step-up (months 4-12): commit increases spread across Q4/Q1 to cover forecasted uplift. Step-ups inked as explicit commit tranches (see table in attached proposal_terms_draft.docx).
- One-time onboarding credit: $60,000 credit to offset initial burst and migration costs (applied to invoice as a credit).
- Overage treatment: overages billed at tiered post-commit rate; credits offset up to first $30k of overage in months 1-2.

Attachments: usage_report_Jul2027.csv (your recent consumption), proposal_terms_draft.docx (draft amendment language and stepped-commit table).

Ask: can you confirm whether procurement will want our standard PO or a short amendment + PO? If procurement prefers an executive summary / MAP, I can send a one-pager and loop in legal.

Next steps:
- If this structure looks reasonable I’ll loop in Kimberly (Sales Ops) to build a final ops model and Rafael for approval of the credit concession. If you need different credit sizing we can adjust quickly.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Manager | Redwood Inference

1) How does the $60k credit apply to overage vs. one-off migration invoices? We need the accounting treatment (credit applied to invoice vs. bill-back).
2) For the staged step-up: can you show the monthly ramp in absolute units (tokens / reserve capacity) instead of only % tranches? Our finance team models in absolute capacity.
3) Procurement asked for a Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and a PO template (attached). Can you provide a one-page MAP they can attach to the PO?

We can be flexible on the ramp cadence but need clarity on invoice timing and any contract-side language that limits our ability to burst. Also — if we commit to a higher tranche earlier than forecast, is there an option to apply the remaining credits to future months?

Folks — forwarding Jason's reply (below). Procurement wants a MAP + PO timeline and needs the credit / overage accounting spelled out.

My read / suggested options:
- Option A (conservative): Keep $60k onboarding credit, apply as an invoice-level credit (applies to first invoice after amendment). Offer a 6% transient renewal concession across the first 3 months (effectively increases value of credit). Step-up commits expressed in absolute tokens: Month 4 add 7T tokens/month reserve, Month 7 add 12T tokens/month reserve, Month 10 add 18T tokens/month reserve.
- Option B (growth-first): Increase credit to $85k, reduce transient discount to 3%, allow unused credits to roll into months 4-6 as overage offset. Legal will need explicit language if credits can be carried forward.

I think Option A is defensible from a cost perspective and easier for finance to model. Rafael — do we have latitude to push to Option B if they insist?

Kimberly — can you run a quick ops model (3 scenarios: baseline, +25% burst, +60% burst) and return an estimate of the unit economics and the incremental GPU-hour exposure so we can finalize the amendment? I’ve attached the customer's usage for July and the draft terms.

If legal needs a redline I can prepare a short amendment; would like to get a MAP + one-pager in the customer's hands by EOD Friday.

Thanks,
Marissa

All — ran the numbers across three scenarios and attached an ops model (ops_model_greenline.xlsx). Quick summary and recommended approach: 

Summary (high level)
- Baseline (no burst): existing spend trajectory, no material change in GPU-hour exposure.
- +25% burst: one-time additional GPU-hours; our marginal cost estimated ~ $0.018/token after batching/kv-cache optimizations.
- +60% burst: sustained increased GPU-hour consumption that would require short-term burst capacity (estimated incremental infra spend ~ $42k over 3 months).

Recommended commercial concession (balanced):
- Keep the temporary shelf (months 0-3) at current rates.
- Offer 6% transient discount applied to invoice(s) in months 0-3.
- One-time credit: $50,000 applied as invoice credit (applies to first invoice post-amendment).
- Step-up commits (absolute): Month 4 add +7,000M tokens/month reserve, Month 7 add +12,000M tokens/month reserve.
- Overage handling: overages billed at step-up tier rate; unused credits do not auto-roll (legal prefers explicit carry-forward language; if customer asks we can allow carry-forward up to 60 days).

Rationale: reduces upfront credit while giving Greenline predictable economics and protects Redwood from sustained burst exposure. The numbers in ops_model_greenline.xlsx show expected unit economics and the downside in worst-case 60% scenario.

Next steps (ops/legal)
- Rafael: please confirm approval to present the 6% + $50k credit (I put an approval checkbox in the ops model).
- Marissa: if Rafael signs off I’ll draft the MAP one-pager and coordinate with Legal for a short amendment / DocuSign.

Happy to jump on a quick 20-min call with Greenline if they want line-by-line.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
